mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an active monetary easing cycle that lowers discount rates for equity valuation, directly increasing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days without regime dependency.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS declines, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in FEDFUNDS exceeding 0.25 percentage points triggers aggressive monetary easing, compressing risk-free rates and boosting equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS falls > 0.25pp in 1 month, 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous increases in PAYEMS (employment) and decreases in UNRATE (unemployment) indicate a tightening labor market that drives consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS rises and UNRATE falls simultaneously, 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In high-inflation, high-growth regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% and GDPC1 growth > 2.0% annually), strong consumer demand drives corporate revenue growth, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In high inflation/high growth regimes, 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) indicate strengthening residential demand, which correlates with increased consumer confidence and corporate investment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days without regime conditions.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST rises, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% signals robust consumer spending, which typically accelerates corporate revenue growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS rises > 0.5% in 1 month, 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in INDPRO (industrial production) and GDPC1 (GDP) indicates expanding supply capacity, which supports corporate profit growth and generates positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO and GDPC1 both rise, 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of cases, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO exceeding 1.0% signals supply chain contraction, reducing corporate output capacity and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO falls > 1.0% in 1 month, 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of cases, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.
